html:
The Idrisids were the first Muslim dynasty to rule Morocco, from 788 to 974. They are shown here in 800 and 900. The map calls their state a caliphate, but they ruled as imams and never claimed the caliph's title.

The founder, Idris I, was a descendant of the Prophet's grandson Hasan. He fled the Abbasids after a failed revolt in Arabia in 786 and reached northern Morocco, where the Awraba Berbers of Volubilis made him their leader in 788. The Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid is said to have had him poisoned in 791.

His son Idris II built up Fez as the capital, and Arab refugees from Kairouan and Córdoba settled there. In 859 Fatima al-Fihri founded the mosque of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, later a great university. After Idris II the realm was divided among his sons and weakened. It became a battleground between the Fatimids and the Umayyads of Córdoba, who ended the dynasty in 974. Many Moroccan families still claim Idrisid descent.
